name: Gazebo Sim (gz-sim)
summary: Current-generation Gazebo robotics simulator with pluggable physics, rendering and a large sensor library (IMU, GPS/NavSat, lidar, cameras, magnetometer, altimeter). Successor to Gazebo Classic.
why_it_matters: The default SITL backend for both PX4 and ArduPilot today; the place to inject sensor noise, GNSS dropouts and degraded conditions into a full autopilot stack.
hackathon_notes: Install a binary release (Harmonic or later) plus ros_gz. Pair with PX4 'make px4_sitl gz_x500' or ardupilot_gazebo. GPU helps for camera sensors; headless server mode works for CI.

name: ros_gz bridge
summary: Bridge packages that relay topics, services and clock between Gazebo Sim transport and ROS 1/ROS 2.
why_it_matters: Needed whenever a ROS 2 navigation or SLAM stack has to consume simulated sensor streams from Gazebo.
hackathon_notes: Use parameter_bridge with a YAML of topic mappings. Match the ros_gz branch to your ROS 2 distro and Gazebo release or builds fail.

name: PX4 SITL Gazebo Classic plugins
summary: Plugins, vehicle models and worlds that connect PX4 SITL/HITL to Gazebo Classic, including GPS, IMU, magnetometer, barometer and optical-flow plugins.
why_it_matters: Large existing corpus of tutorials and research setups still target it; the GPS plugin is a common starting point for spoofing and jamming experiments in sim.
hackathon_notes: Works with Ubuntu 20.04/22.04 and Gazebo 11. Gazebo Classic has reached end of life, so prefer gz-sim for new builds unless you need a specific legacy model.

name: PX4 Gazebo models
summary: Model and world repository for the new Gazebo, used by PX4 SITL targets such as gz_x500.
why_it_matters: Shows how PX4 vehicles and sensors are described for gz-sim; the starting point for adding custom sensors to a PX4 airframe.
hackathon_notes: Fetched automatically by PX4 SITL. Fork and edit SDF to add cameras or change sensor noise.

name: jMAVSim
summary: Lightweight Java multirotor simulator that speaks MAVLink to PX4, without a 3D-world physics engine.
why_it_matters: Was the fastest way to get a PX4 SITL quad flying for MAVLink, GCS or mission-logic work when sensors and worlds do not matter; PX4 has since replaced it with SIH.
hackathon_notes: Removed from PX4-Autopilot main in September 2026; 'make px4_sitl jmavsim' only exists up to PX4 v1.17. On current PX4 use 'make px4_sitl_sih sihsim_quadx' with Hawkeye. Needs a JDK. No cameras or lidar, so not for perception work. This repo is PX4's fork of DrTon/jMAVSim.

name: ArduPilot Gazebo plugin
summary: Plugins and models connecting ArduPilot SITL to Gazebo Sim over the JSON SITL interface.
why_it_matters: Brings ArduPilot vehicles (copter, plane, rover, boat) into gz-sim with realistic sensors for nav and autonomy testing.
hackathon_notes: Build against your Gazebo release, run sim_vehicle.py with '-f gazebo-iris --model JSON'. Follow the README's environment variables for model paths.

name: ArduPilot SITL Models
summary: Collection of aircraft and vehicle models and parameter files for ArduPilot SITL, mostly for the RealFlight simulator (planes, quadplanes, tailsitters, helicopters, multicopters) plus a Gazebo package with models and worlds.
why_it_matters: Ready-made airframes (including fixed-wing and VTOL) save hours when a hackathon scenario needs something other than a quadcopter.
hackathon_notes: No top-level README. RealFlight is a paid commercial simulator; without it, only the Gazebo folder is usable. RealFlight model folders each have their own README.

name: AirSim
summary: Unreal Engine based simulator for drones and cars with camera, depth, lidar, IMU, GPS, barometer and magnetometer models and a Python/C++ API. Microsoft wound down development and pointed users to Project AirSim.
why_it_matters: Still the most widely used photorealistic drone sim in research papers; many visual-nav and geolocalization datasets were rendered with it.
hackathon_notes: Prebuilt binary environments are the quickest path. Building from source requires a matching old Unreal version. For new work prefer Colosseum or Project AirSim.

name: Colosseum (AirSim fork)
summary: Community fork of AirSim that moved it to newer Unreal Engine 5 releases. The GitHub repository is now marked archived.
why_it_matters: Was the main path to run AirSim on UE5; useful as a reference port even though it is no longer maintained.
hackathon_notes: Archived on GitHub, so expect unanswered issues. Use only if you need its UE5 changes specifically.

name: Project AirSim
summary: Open-source release of Project AirSim, the rewrite and successor of AirSim, for building and testing autonomous aerial systems in high-fidelity Unreal environments.
why_it_matters: The actively developed line of the AirSim family, relevant for photorealistic aerial perception and autonomy testing.
hackathon_notes: Check its docs for supported Unreal version and OS. Heavier setup than AirSim binaries; budget several hours.

name: Flightmare
summary: Quadrotor simulator from UZH RPG with a decoupled Unity renderer and fast dynamics, aimed at RL and vision-based agile flight.
why_it_matters: Lets you train vision-based or state-based quadrotor policies with many parallel environments.
hackathon_notes: Last updated 2024 and ROS1-oriented; expect dependency fixing. Unity renderer binaries are separate downloads.

name: FlightGoggles
summary: Unity3D and ROS framework from MIT for photorealistic camera rendering with real or simulated vehicle dynamics in the loop.
why_it_matters: Pioneered vehicle-in-the-loop rendering: fly a real drone in a mocap room while feeding it synthetic imagery.
hackathon_notes: Not actively maintained since 2024; ROS1. Mostly of interest as a reference or alongside the Blackbird dataset.

name: Pegasus Simulator
summary: Framework on top of NVIDIA Isaac Sim for simulating multirotors with PX4 in the loop and Python-defined vehicles and sensors.
why_it_matters: Gives PX4 users photorealistic, GPU-accelerated Omniverse rendering while keeping the real autopilot stack.
hackathon_notes: Needs an RTX GPU and an Isaac Sim install; match Pegasus release to the Isaac Sim version listed in its docs.

name: NVIDIA Isaac Sim
summary: NVIDIA's Omniverse-based robot simulator, now open source, with RTX sensor simulation (cameras, lidar, IMU) and ROS 2 bridges.
why_it_matters: Base layer for Pegasus, OmniDrones and Isaac Lab; strong for synthetic data generation for perception models.
hackathon_notes: RTX GPU and a lot of disk required. Use the prebuilt container or pip install rather than building from source in a hackathon.

name: Isaac Lab
summary: Robot-learning framework on Isaac Sim for massively parallel RL and imitation learning, with navigation and locomotion task examples.
why_it_matters: Fast route to training learned navigation or locomotion policies with thousands of parallel simulated robots.
hackathon_notes: Install via pip on a supported Isaac Sim version. Start from an existing nav task config rather than writing environments from scratch.

name: CARLA
summary: Open-source autonomous-driving simulator on Unreal with camera, lidar, radar, GNSS and IMU sensors, traffic and weather control.
why_it_matters: Standard ground-vehicle testbed for localization and planning under weather, night and sensor-degradation conditions.
hackathon_notes: Use packaged releases and the Python client; the ROS 2 bridge is separate. A decent GPU is required.

name: RotorS
summary: Gazebo Classic MAV simulator from ETH ASL with multirotor models, IMU and odometry sensor plugins and example controllers.
why_it_matters: Classic reference for MAV sim used in many VIO and planning papers; its IMU noise models are still frequently copied.
hackathon_notes: ROS1 and Gazebo Classic only; use for reproducing older papers rather than new builds.

name: Aerial Gym Simulator
summary: GPU-parallel aerial-robot simulator from NTNU ARL built on NVIDIA Isaac Gym, with depth/range sensors and RL navigation examples.
why_it_matters: Train learned obstacle avoidance and navigation for drones at scale with simulated depth cameras and lidar.
hackathon_notes: Needs NVIDIA GPU and Isaac Gym preview (a legacy package); check README for current install path.

name: gym-pybullet-drones
summary: Gymnasium environments on PyBullet for single and multi-agent quadcopter control and RL (formerly under utiasDSL).
why_it_matters: Lowest-friction multi-drone RL sandbox: pure Python, CPU-only, quick to modify.
hackathon_notes: pip install in a venv and run examples within minutes. No photorealistic sensors; good for control, swarming and planning logic.

name: OmniDrones
summary: GPU-parallel drone simulation and RL platform built on Isaac Sim.
why_it_matters: Supports multi-drone and transport tasks with vectorized environments for learning-based autonomy.
hackathon_notes: Pinned to specific Isaac Sim versions (README badge: 4.1.0) and Linux only. The author states at the top of the README that this version is hard to maintain and will not be updated further; treat it as frozen.

name: RotorPy
summary: Python multirotor simulator with aerodynamic effects (drag, wind) for education and research.
why_it_matters: Good for studying estimator and controller behaviour under wind and disturbances without a game engine.
hackathon_notes: pip installable, runs on a laptop. Has IMU and mocap-style sensor models; add your own estimator in Python.

name: Webots
summary: General-purpose open-source robot simulator with many robot models and sensors including GPS, compass, IMU, lidar and radar.
why_it_matters: Cross-platform and easy to install; good for ground and multi-robot nav demos with ROS 2 integration.
hackathon_notes: Installers for Windows, macOS and Linux. webots_ros2 package for ROS 2. Less common in aerial autonomy.

name: Stonefish
summary: C++ simulation library for marine robotics with hydrodynamics and underwater sensors such as DVL, sonars, pressure, IMU and cameras.
why_it_matters: One of the few open sims with credible underwater nav sensors for AUV dead reckoning and sonar-based localization work.
hackathon_notes: Use with stonefish_ros or stonefish_ros2. Requires OpenGL 4.3 capable GPU.

name: HoloOcean (documentation)
summary: Documentation repository for HoloOcean, BYU's Unreal-based underwater simulator with sonar, DVL, IMU, depth and camera sensors and multi-agent support. The simulator code itself is not hosted in this repo.
why_it_matters: Photorealistic underwater sim aimed at marine navigation and SLAM research, including acoustic modems for multi-agent setups.
hackathon_notes: Follow the installation page of the docs; Python package plus downloadable worlds. Heavy GPU load for sonar rendering.

name: Project DAVE
summary: Gazebo-based underwater simulation environment with sensor plugins (multibeam sonar, DVL) and UUV models, building on UUV Simulator.
why_it_matters: Useful starting point for underwater navigation testing with DVL and sonar in a ROS stack.
hackathon_notes: Last updated 2024 and ROS1/Gazebo Classic based; Docker is the realistic path.

name: UUV Simulator
summary: Gazebo/ROS packages for unmanned underwater vehicles with hydrodynamics and thrusters. Archived on GitHub.
why_it_matters: Many underwater-nav papers and DAVE build on it; useful for reference models.
hackathon_notes: Archived and tied to old ROS/Gazebo; use Stonefish or DAVE instead.

name: Virtual RobotX (VRX)
summary: Simulation environment for the RobotX maritime challenge with a WAM-V surface vessel, waves, wind and GPS/IMU/camera/lidar sensors.
why_it_matters: Ready-made surface-vessel sim with nav and perception tasks; good for maritime autonomy demos.
hackathon_notes: Current branch targets gz-sim and ROS 2. Task worlds (station keeping, wayfinding) work as hackathon challenges out of the box.

name: GRID playground (AirGen)
summary: Notes and examples for the GRID platform from General Robotics (formerly Scaled Foundations), which pairs the AirSim-derived AirGen simulator with foundation-model perception and LLM-driven robot control.
why_it_matters: Shows a sim plus foundation-model workflow for aerial autonomy, close to 'LLM in the loop' hackathon ideas.
hackathon_notes: Uses the hosted GRID platform for the sim side; check account requirements before relying on it.

name: JSBSim
summary: Open-source flight dynamics model library for fixed-wing and other aircraft, used by FlightGear and as an ArduPilot SITL backend.
why_it_matters: Credible fixed-wing dynamics for testing navigation filters on aircraft profiles rather than quadcopters.
hackathon_notes: Python bindings via pip. Combine with ArduPilot SITL for an autopilot loop.

name: MARSIM
summary: Lightweight point-realistic lidar simulator for UAVs from HKU MaRS, supporting rotating and solid-state lidar patterns.
why_it_matters: Fast way to test lidar-based UAV navigation and planning without a full game-engine sim.
hackathon_notes: ROS based; runs on CPU or modest GPU. Pairs well with FAST-LIO-style stacks.

name: ESIM
summary: Event camera simulator from UZH RPG that renders event streams from simulated scenes.
why_it_matters: Generates event-camera data for high-speed or low-light VIO research without hardware.
hackathon_notes: ROS1 and older build tooling. For converting existing video to events, rpg_vid2e is easier.

name: gnss-ins-sim
summary: Python GNSS/INS simulator that generates trajectories, IMU/GNSS/magnetometer measurements with configurable error models, and runs navigation algorithms on them.
why_it_matters: Quick way to produce synthetic IMU and GNSS data with known truth to test filters and dead reckoning under GNSS outage.
hackathon_notes: Pure Python; define a motion profile CSV and IMU grade, then run. Last updated 2024 but stable.

name: evo
summary: Python package and CLI for evaluating and plotting odometry and SLAM trajectories (APE, RPE) across TUM, KITTI, EuRoC and ROS bag formats.
why_it_matters: The default way to score a nav or SLAM result against ground truth; essential for any demo that claims accuracy.
hackathon_notes: pip install evo. Run evo_ape with alignment flags; it reads most dataset ground-truth formats directly.

name: rpg_trajectory_evaluation
summary: Toolbox from UZH RPG for quantitative VO/VIO trajectory evaluation with several alignment modes and multi-run statistics.
why_it_matters: Implements the alignment conventions used in many VIO benchmarks; good for apples-to-apples comparisons.
hackathon_notes: Old Python 2 era code, ROS optional. evo is easier for quick use.

name: pykitti
summary: Python loaders for the KITTI raw and odometry datasets.
why_it_matters: Removes boilerplate when using KITTI's GPS/IMU, lidar and stereo data for localization experiments.
hackathon_notes: pip install pykitti and point it at the dataset folders.

name: UZH-FPV dataset tools
summary: Companion repo for the UZH-FPV drone racing dataset with scripts and info.
why_it_matters: Aggressive high-speed drone sequences stress VIO well beyond EuRoC.
hackathon_notes: Inactive since 2020; dataset itself is on the UZH site under CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (non-commercial). The repo code is GPL-3.0.

name: Hilti SLAM Challenge 2022
summary: Repository for the 2022 Hilti SLAM Challenge with dataset info and evaluation tooling.
why_it_matters: Construction-site sequences with accurate ground truth; a strong test of lidar/visual-inertial SLAM in GNSS-denied indoor spaces.
hackathon_notes: Bags are on the challenge site and Hugging Face (Hilti-Research/hilti-slam-challenge-2022); ground truth and evaluation scripts are in the repo. Data licence is CC BY-NC-SA 3.0: non-commercial use only.

name: Hilti SLAM Challenge 2023
summary: Repository for the 2023 Hilti SLAM Challenge, including multi-session sequences.
why_it_matters: Multi-session data is useful for map reuse and relocalization experiments.
hackathon_notes: Same workflow as 2022; bags on the challenge site and Hugging Face. Data licence is CC BY-NC-SA 3.0: non-commercial use only.

name: MCD: Multi-Campus Dataset
summary: Site repo for MCD, a multi-campus dataset across Asia and Europe with spinning and non-repetitive lidar, stereo cameras, IMUs, UWB ranging, survey-grade prior maps and continuous-time ground truth.
why_it_matters: Covers localization against prior maps and UWB-aided fusion in large outdoor areas.
hackathon_notes: Data downloads and tutorials are linked from the site. Licensed CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, intended for non-commercial academic use.

name: NTU VIRAL dataset
summary: Site repo for NTU VIRAL, an aerial dataset with lidars, cameras, IMU and UWB ranging from a drone.
why_it_matters: Rare UWB-equipped drone dataset for range-aided fusion experiments.
hackathon_notes: ROS bags; download links on the site. Licensed CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 for non-commercial academic use; commercial use needs contact with the authors.

name: M2DGR
summary: Multi-modal, multi-scenario ground robot dataset from SJTU with cameras, lidar, IMU, GNSS and more, indoor and outdoor.
why_it_matters: Indoor/outdoor transitions with GNSS make it useful for testing GNSS-loss handling in fusion.
hackathon_notes: ROS bags; check repo for download mirrors. Repo says MIT but the dataset is 'provided for academic purpose'; commercial use requires contacting the authors.

name: GVINS dataset
summary: Dataset with synchronized visual, inertial and raw GNSS measurements released with GVINS.
why_it_matters: One of few datasets with raw GNSS pseudoranges plus camera and IMU, needed for tightly coupled GNSS-VIO.
hackathon_notes: ROS bags with custom GNSS message types; install the gnss_comm package. Dataset licence is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (non-commercial).

name: UrbanNav
summary: Open multisensor urban positioning dataset from PolyU IPNL with GNSS, IMU, lidar and camera in deep urban canyons.
why_it_matters: Benchmark for GNSS multipath and NLOS mitigation in cities.
hackathon_notes: Pick one Hong Kong sequence and run an RTKLIB plus loosely coupled baseline to show urban degradation.

name: ALTO
summary: Placeholder repo for ALTO, an aerial-view, large-scale, terrain-oriented dataset for UAV place recognition and localization. It holds only a README with Dropbox links to the ICRA 2022 GPR Competition rounds; the full dataset is still marked 'Coming soon'.
why_it_matters: Directly targets UAV localization over terrain when GNSS is unavailable.
hackathon_notes: Inactive since 2022; only the competition subsets are downloadable (Dropbox), so check the links still work before planning around it. The BSD-3 licence covers the repo; no data terms are stated.

name: VPAIR
summary: Repo for VPAIR, an aerial visual place recognition dataset matching low-altitude flight imagery to reference orthophotos.
why_it_matters: Benchmark for UAV visual geolocalization against georeferenced maps.
hackathon_notes: Academic use only, commercial use prohibited (README). Full set is 20.5 GB (2,706 query/reference pairs plus 10,000 distractors); a 0.86 GB sample is on Zenodo. The repo itself holds only the README and images. Evaluate with VPR-methods-evaluation.

name: UAV-VisLoc
summary: Large-scale dataset of UAV images paired with satellite maps for absolute visual localization.
why_it_matters: Fits the 'locate the drone from its camera and a satellite map' GNSS-denied scenario.
hackathon_notes: Dataset only, no baseline code; pair with a feature matcher or VPR model.

name: University-1652
summary: Benchmark and baseline code for drone-based geolocalization with drone, satellite and ground views of university buildings.
why_it_matters: Most cited drone-to-satellite cross-view benchmark; baselines train on a single GPU.
hackathon_notes: Request dataset access via the form in README early - it is not instant.

name: SUES-200
summary: Cross-view drone-satellite benchmark with images at multiple flight heights and scene types.
why_it_matters: Lets you measure how cross-view geolocalization degrades with altitude.
hackathon_notes: Comparable training pipeline to University-1652. The dataset is for academic research only, despite the repo's MIT code licence.

name: DenseUAV
summary: Dataset and baseline for vision-based UAV self-positioning in low-altitude urban environments (TIP 2023).
why_it_matters: Frames geolocalization as dense position estimation rather than building retrieval.
hackathon_notes: Baseline is PyTorch; GPU needed for training.

name: AerialVL
summary: Visual geo-localization dataset and code designed for aerial vehicles.
why_it_matters: Another aerial-to-map benchmark with sequential flights, useful for testing filtering over VPR outputs.
hackathon_notes: Check README for map tile download steps.

name: Mapillary SLS
summary: Tools for the Mapillary Street-level Sequences dataset for lifelong visual place recognition.
why_it_matters: Large, diverse street-level VPR benchmark used to train many current VPR models.
hackathon_notes: Dataset download needs registration on Mapillary.

name: VPR-Bench
summary: Open-source visual place recognition evaluation framework from the IJCV paper, with many datasets and techniques integrated.
why_it_matters: Ready harness to compare VPR methods across conditions and viewpoints.
hackathon_notes: Older dependencies; consider VPR-methods-evaluation for modern models. Bundled datasets and techniques keep their own licences (see each folder); the MIT licence covers the framework code only.

name: VPR-methods-evaluation
summary: Wrapper to run and evaluate many state-of-the-art VPR models on any image database/query split by changing one parameter.
why_it_matters: Quickest way to get a strong VPR baseline on your own aerial or street imagery.
hackathon_notes: Format your data as database/queries folders with UTM in filenames; GPU recommended.

name: tartanairpy
summary: Python package for downloading, customizing and iterating the TartanAir-V2 synthetic dataset.
why_it_matters: TartanAir's photorealistic scenes with weather and lighting variety stress-test SLAM and VO.
hackathon_notes: Download only the environments and modalities you need - full set is very large.

name: pyboreas
summary: Devkit for the Boreas multi-season driving dataset with radar, lidar, camera and GNSS/INS ground truth.
why_it_matters: Radar plus lidar over seasons and snow suits all-weather localization work.
hackathon_notes: Data is hosted on S3; download selected sequences.

name: Oxford RobotCar SDK
summary: SDK for the Oxford RobotCar dataset with loaders and projection tools.
why_it_matters: Long-term, all-condition driving data is a staple for localization and place recognition research.
hackathon_notes: Inactive since 2022; Python and MATLAB helpers still work. The dataset itself is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, for non-commercial academic use only.

name: Blackbird dataset
summary: MIT dataset of aggressive indoor quadrotor flights with real IMU and motor data and rendered camera imagery.
why_it_matters: Combines real flight dynamics with synthetic vision, good for VIO under aggressive motion.
hackathon_notes: Inactive since 2022; download scripts may need adaptation.

name: GPS Measurement Tools
summary: Google's tools for logging and analysing raw GNSS measurements from Android phones, including the GnssLogger app and MATLAB analysis code.
why_it_matters: Basis for collecting your own smartphone raw GNSS data, the same format as the Smartphone Decimeter Challenge.
hackathon_notes: Install GnssLogger on an Android phone and log raw measurements during the event.

name: GSDC 2023 solution (taroz)
summary: Published solution code for the Google Smartphone Decimeter Challenge 2023 by Taro Suzuki.
why_it_matters: Strong reference pipeline for precise smartphone GNSS positioning.
hackathon_notes: MATLAB required. Read it for the pipeline design even if you reimplement in Python.

name: MagNav.jl
summary: Julia package for airborne magnetic anomaly navigation, released with the MagNav challenge data and baseline models.
why_it_matters: The open entry point to the AFRL/MIT magnetic navigation challenge data.
hackathon_notes: Julia install required, or use the provided Docker image; data downloads via the package's artifacts. The flight data is under a US Air Force Data Sharing Agreement: non-profit research, non-profit education or US government purposes only.
